key_insight: Chimera shows that a hybrid attention design can scale visual diffusion models to much larger image/video contexts without the quadratic cost of full attention. Its key idea is to mix efficient long-context memory with latent attention in a unified raster-order token stream.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the computational bottleneck of full self-attention in visual generation, especially for high-resolution images, long videos, and multimodal inputs where token counts become very large.
method: Uses a hybrid visual diffusion backbone that processes text, image, and video tokens together in one raster-ordered stream.
Removes the need for positional embeddings by relying on the stream structure and attention design.
Combines Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for O(N) long-context state tracking with interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) for efficient representation.
impact: For practitioners, Chimera points to a practical path for training and scaling visual generative models more efficiently at high resolution and long duration. It can reduce memory/compute pressure while preserving the ability to model long-range dependencies across multimodal content.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing text, image, and video tokens merged into one raster-ordered stream.

A scaling chart illustrating improved efficiency as token length increases.
paper_title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers
paper_authors: Chongjian Ge, Hanwen Jiang, Tianyu Wang, Jiuxiang Gu, Yiran Xu
